groups.title: Quantum chemistry
groups.blurb: Hartree–Fock from the Gaussian integrals up, with the published energies to compare against.

groups.title: Plasma physics
groups.blurb: Kinetic and fluid plasma: Landau damping, drift-wave turbulence, tokamak equilibrium, transport coefficients.

groups.title: Nuclear & astrophysics
groups.blurb: Neutron-star structure and nuclear level densities by exact counting.

groups.title: Numerical methods
groups.blurb: Finite elements, molecular dynamics, a spectral Poisson solve, and the records refactor of the FEM solver.

groups.title: Automatic differentiation
groups.blurb: Forward mode by dual numbers, reverse mode by tape, and deriv() — AD as a compiler transform.

groups.title: Symbolic computation & discovery
groups.blurb: A computer-algebra system on flat arrays, symbolic regression, Meijer-G metamodeling, symmetry discovery.

groups.title: Language features
groups.blurb: The minimal demos: arithmetic and functions; control flow and recursion.

programs.title: annotated
programs.blurb: The worked example for the native-annotation syntax: the Boys function and the primitive Gaussian overlap from the SCF programs, annotated at all three levels, with two labeled regions and a variable glossary.

programs.title: area
programs.blurb: A few numeric functions, in real Viv syntax.

programs.title: autodiff deriv
programs.blurb: Automatic forward-mode AD: `deriv(fn(x) -> expr, x0)` returns the EXACT derivative d/dx expr at x0 -- the compiler dualizes the expression (chain rule over + - * /, exp, sqrt, pow), so no dual arithmetic is written by hand.

programs.title: autodiff forward
programs.blurb: Forward-mode automatic differentiation via dual numbers.

programs.title: autodiff reverse
programs.blurb: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation via a tape ("micrograd in Viv").

programs.title: control
programs.blurb: Control flow: recursion, while, for, break/continue, if/else.

programs.title: debye SCF
programs.blurb: Self-consistent field solution of the nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann equation for Debye screening of a charged wall in a plasma: the classical mean-field cousin of the Hartree-Fock SCF (scf_sto3g.viv).

programs.title: FEM poisson
programs.blurb: Finite-element solution of the 2D Poisson equation -Laplacian(u) = f on the unit square with u = 0 on the boundary, using linear (P1) triangular elements.

programs.title: FEM poisson records
programs.blurb: The 2D Poisson FEM (see fem_poisson.viv), refactored with records to show the named-field bundling that motivated them: the mesh is a single `Mesh` value passed to functions (instead of three loose global arrays), and each element's geometry is a `Tri` value passed to helpers (instead of nine loose scalars).

programs.title: fft poisson
programs.blurb: Poisson's equation, solved spectrally: -u'' = f on a periodic domain.

programs.title: fused views
programs.blurb: Elementwise expressions and reductions over slices, as the compiled engines fuse them (lang/viv/src/fuse.rs): every result is compared to the element loop that writes the same arithmetic in the same order, to the bit.

programs.title: geomopt
programs.blurb: Geometry optimization by numerical gradients: relax a diatomic's bond length to its equilibrium by finding where the RHF/STO-3G energy is stationary.

programs.title: geomopt water
programs.blurb: Polyatomic geometry optimization: relax water (H2O) to its equilibrium by numerical-gradient Newton on the RHF/STO-3G energy surface.

programs.title: grad shafranov
programs.blurb: Grad-Shafranov equilibrium of a tokamak: the self-consistent MHD force balance J x B = grad p, written for the poloidal flux psi(R,Z).

programs.title: h2 STO3G
programs.blurb: Restricted Hartree-Fock for H2 at fixed geometry in the STO-3G basis.

programs.title: hasegawa wakatani
programs.blurb: Hasegawa-Wakatani (1983): resistive drift-wave turbulence.

programs.title: hchain STO3G
programs.blurb: Restricted Hartree-Fock for a linear chain of N hydrogen atoms in STO-3G.

programs.title: level density
programs.blurb: Nuclear level density by exact many-fermion state counting.

programs.title: MD polymer
programs.blurb: Molecular dynamics of a Lennard-Jones bead-spring polymer.

programs.title: meijer g
programs.blurb: Symbolic metamodeling by continuous optimization: the Meijer G-function trick of Alaa & van der Schaar (NeurIPS 2019), in Viv.

programs.title: mini CAS
programs.blurb: A mini computer-algebra system in Viv: symbolic computation written with no pointers, no strings and no Int values, only arrays of numbers.

programs.title: NN symmetry
programs.blurb: NN-guided symmetry discovery: the AI-Feynman outer loop, in Viv.

programs.title: oneil trapping
programs.blurb: O'Neil (1965) trapping: the nonlinear sequel to Landau damping.

programs.title: SCF mcmurchie
programs.blurb: Restricted Hartree-Fock with a general McMurchie-Davidson integral engine, supporting s AND p Cartesian Gaussians (extends to higher angular momentum).

programs.title: SCF STO3G
programs.blurb: Molecule-driven restricted Hartree-Fock in STO-3G.

programs.title: SCF water
programs.blurb: Restricted Hartree-Fock for WATER (H2O) in STO-3G, with a general McMurchie-Davidson integral engine over s AND p Cartesian Gaussians.

programs.title: SCF water 631GD
programs.blurb: Restricted Hartree-Fock for WATER (H2O) in 6-31G(d) [6-31G*], with a general McMurchie-Davidson integral engine over s, p, AND d Cartesian Gaussians.

programs.title: spitzer harm
programs.blurb: Spitzer-Harm (1953) conductivity: the electrical conductivity of a fully ionized plasma from the linearized Fokker-Planck collision operator.

programs.title: symbolic regression
programs.blurb: Symbolic regression in Viv: recover a formula from data by brute force.

programs.title: TOV
programs.blurb: Neutron-star structure from the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, with the relativistic free neutron-gas equation of state.

programs.title: two stream pic
programs.blurb: The two-stream instability by a 1D electrostatic particle-in-cell (PIC) code: the kinetic model in its rawest form -- push real particles, let them make their own field, and watch a beam-plasma instability grow out of noise.

programs.title: vlasov landau
programs.blurb: Landau damping by a 1D1V Vlasov-Poisson solver, written in Viv.

programs.title: xyz atoms
programs.blurb: Read a molecule written as XYZ text into atoms: symbol, atomic number, position (the parser is lib/xyz.viv).
